title: A GOOD REPORT MEETS A FEARFUL HEART

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They came back to Moses and Aaron and the whole Israelite community at Kadesh in the Desert of Paran. There they reported to them and to the whole assembly and showed them the fruit of the land. They gave Moses this account: "We went into the land to which you sent us, and it does flow with milk and honey! Here is its fruit. But the people who live there are powerful, and the cities are fortified and very large. We even saw descendants of Anak there. The Amalekites live in the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live near the sea and along the Jordan." — Num 13:26-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The report begins so well. "It does flow with milk and honey!" they say, holding up the fruit. Everything God promised is confirmed with their own eyes. But then comes the fatal little word: "But." "But the people are powerful, the cities are fortified, and we saw giants."

That "but" is where faith so often collapses. We acknowledge God's goodness, we admit His promises are true — and then we let one small word turn all our attention to the obstacles. "God is faithful, but this problem is so big." "The Lord is good, but look at my circumstances." The "but" quietly puts the giants on the throne where God belongs.

The ten spies were not lying. Every fact in their report was accurate. The land was good; the people were strong. Their sin was not in the facts but in the framing — they placed the obstacles in the foreground and pushed God into the background. They had left the most important factor out of their calculation entirely: the Lord who had promised the land.

We can be truthful and faithless at the same time. It is possible to state every fact correctly and still leave God out of the equation. The remedy is to keep rehearsing the greater truth: the Lord who promised is faithful, and no giant is bigger than Him. When the "but" rises in your heart, answer it with a greater "but God."

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How often does a fearful "but" undo your confidence in God's goodness?
2. Is it possible to state facts truthfully yet leave God out of the picture?
3. What "but God" truth do you need to rehearse over your fears today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the fearful "but" that so often pushes You into the background. Help me to keep You at the centre of every situation, and to answer my fears with the greater truth of who You are. Amen.
